plan: My goal is to maximize profit. Given my value is $9, I need to consider how much to bid to win without overpaying. The "price to win" is the highest bid of others. If I bid $9, I guarantee a profit if I win. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above what I expect the other bidders to bid, but not more than my value. Since this is the first round and I have no history, I will bid a conservative amount, slightly above what a very low-value bidder might bid, but still less than my value. I will bid $7.50.

I need to maximize profit. My value is $40. I want to win if I can pay less than $40. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value. This ensures that I win if and only if my value is greater than the highest competing bid, and I pay that highest competing bid. This strategy maximizes my expected profit in the long run.
